items.title: An element is a unit exactly when its class modulo a locally nilpotent ideal is a unit
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a ring R with a locally nilpotent ideal I, the lemma states that an element x is a unit exactly when its class in R/I is a unit (statement lines 6496-6502). The proof does not use lifting of units along a nilpotent extension in the abstract: from a class y with xy = 1 - z and z in I it reads the identity as 1 congruent to z modulo the principal ideal generated by x, uses that z is nilpotent, raises the congruence to a high power to obtain 1 congruent to 0 modulo xR, and concludes that x divides 1 (proof lines 6504-6514). Turning nilpotence into the termination of a geometric-series style argument is the substance, and the author writes it out. H2.
